label: Objective / Fact-based
description: Questions with a clear, factual, and verifiable answer.
criteria: There is one correct answer or a small set of known facts.
Answers can be compared for accuracy using exact matching or similarity.
Typically used for technical or knowledge-based questions.

label: Situational / Hypothetical
description: Scenario-based questions where the answer is judged based on reasoning and logic.
criteria: Describes a hypothetical situation (e.g. conflict, project delay).
Has a good vs. poor way to respond, but not a single correct answer.
Answers are evaluated for critical thinking and professionalism.

label: Behavioral / Experience-based
description: Experience-driven questions that ask the user to reflect on past actions.
criteria: Starts with 'Tell me about a time…' or similar.
Answers should describe real actions and outcomes.
Assessed using keywords, relevance, and structure (e.g. STAR method).

label: Soft Skill / Personal Quality
description: Evaluates character traits, habits, or interpersonal skills.
criteria: Focuses on communication, adaptability, strengths/weaknesses, etc.
No clear right or wrong answer, but some are stronger than others.
Scored using tone, keyword alignment, and coherence.

label: Opinion / Personal Preference
description: Subjective questions with no expectations for correctness.
criteria: Meant to explore personality or preferences (e.g. favorite language).
No judgment or scoring beyond tone or appropriateness.
Used for engagement or casual discussion.
